subject: Chemistry
title: Why Milk Curdles
description: Learn Why Milk Curdles in one minute.

hook.text: Add lemon juice to warm milk and it splits into lumps and liquid in seconds. That's cheese starting.

buildup.text: Milk contains casein proteins floating in suspension. They repel each other because of negative charges.

discovery.text: Acid neutralizes the charges. Without repulsion, casein proteins clump together—forming curds.

twist.text: Rennet enzyme does the same thing without acid. It's been used to make cheese for over 7,000 years.

climax.text: Curds become cheese. The liquid whey becomes protein powder. Nothing is wasted.

punchline.text: Acid kills the charge, proteins clump. Milk becomes cheese.

quiz.question: Why does acid make milk curdle?
options: It neutralizes charges on casein proteins so they clump together
It heats the milk from the inside
It kills bacteria that keep milk liquid

details.summary: Milk curdles when its casein proteins lose their stable suspension and clump together. This happens through acid addition, which neutralizes the negative charges keeping protein micelles apart, or through enzymatic action like rennet breaking down kappa-casein..
details.whyItMatters: Milk curdling chemistry is the foundation of the entire cheese-making industry and demonstrates protein denaturation, acid-base interactions, and colloidal chemistry.
takeaways: Acid neutralizes charges on casein micelles, causing them to clump
Rennet enzyme specifically cleaves kappa-casein to trigger coagulation
Spoiled milk curdles because bacteria produce lactic acid from lactose

faq.question: Why does adding lemon juice to hot milk cause it to curdle instantly?
faq.answer: Citric acid in lemon juice lowers the pH toward casein's isoelectric point of 4.6, neutralizing the negative charges that keep casein micelles repelling each other..

faq.question: How does cheese-making control the curdling process?
faq.answer: Cheese makers use specific amounts of acid or rennet enzyme to control curd firmness and moisture content. Temperature, timing, and pH are precisely managed. The whey is drained, and curds are salted, pressed, and aged. Different conditions produce the enormous variety of cheese types.
